summary: Replace the unrelated Ritter reference with the verified Prym–Socin passage

Its preceding verse gives the same conquest context. Replace only 99/114 and retain 253 and prs 163/22.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (PrS 10/56)

data.turoyo: Omər: “Howe ḥaram aʕli ikan kmuhanno an nišani aʕli, d lo mhoro gdumaxno gabayye.”
data.translation: Da sagte er: »Ich will untergehen, wenn ich mir diese Weiber erst antrauen lasse; ich will ohne Trauung sie zu meinen Frauen machen«.

rationale: First Infinitiv example: d lo mhoro contrasts with finite kmuhanno.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (PrS 36/59)

data.turoyo: heš kla i Xənge dlo mhoro.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 4/17)

data.turoyo: Aṯyo lu bayto hiya w huwe w mhərre ḥḏoḏe. W tu šmera zax.
data.translation: sie aber kehrte nach Hause zurück, und sie heirateten einander.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 34/113)

data.turoyo: Maṣlawle lu qašo ʕar riša w mʕamḏole. Mhəlle a tləṯ aʕle.
data.translation: Der Pfaffe liess sie nun beichten und taufte sie, dann traute er ihm die drei Frauen an.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (110/25)

data.turoyo: qayəmno hedika, mhiroli ʕal u zlamawo w kətle uʕdo tre, tloṯo naʕime mena.
data.translation: mit dem verheiratete ich sie, und er hat jetzt zwei, drei Kinder von ihr.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (112/261)

data.turoyo: Ḥḏo mak kačkanək mhirole l Ṭafšo, hala, l Kandilo w ḥḏo mhirole l Bašto.
data.translation: Eines der Mädchen heiratete Tafscho - Verzeihung - Kandilo, und eines Baschto.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 39/100)

data.turoyo: Nšəqle lu paša w mhəlle i xatune aʕme.
data.translation: Da küsste ihn der Fürst und verheiratete die Prinzessin mit ihm;

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Dilo and Falako/12)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Ašə́r gəmbaraxna. Gmohaṇṇa’ — ‘Yămā́n, daxī́l! I+barṯo dan+nayaryo’. Səәәmle, lo+səmle, omar, ‘Lo! Gəmbaraxna’.
data.translation: He says, ‘Really, I’ll bless (i.e., marry) her. I’ll marry her (i.e., in the Muslim fashion)’. — ‘Mercy, help! She’s the enemies’ daughter’. Whatever he did (lit. ‘he did, he didn’t do’), he says, ‘No! I’ll marry her’.

rationale: Distinct heavily assimilated Gmohaṇṇa form and explicit Muslim ceremony gloss.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (95/57)

data.turoyo: ono, d šəqlatli, uʕdo haha gədməblallux l i=odakayḏi, gməhrallux ʕal ruḥi.
data.translation: Wenn du mich nimmst, nehme ich dich jetzt gleich mit in mein Zimmerchen und heirate dich.

rationale: Male object with female acting/arranging spouse; participant extension.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 25/16)

data.turoyo: Gmuhannulxu aʕli, haṯi aṯti yo w haṯi ste gsamna aṯti.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 34/111)

data.turoyo: Maṭi lu bayto l si emo. Fṣiḥo i emo. Qrele lu qašo, omər: "Mhar at tartani aʕli, haṯi ṭayayto yo, lə kməhanna."
data.translation: Nun kam er nach Hause zu seiner Mutter, diese freute sich sehr. Er liess den Pfaffen kommen und sagte ihm: »Traue mir diese beiden an, jene ist eine Mohammedanerin, die heirate ich nicht«.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell with explicit priest as addressee; retain entire short ceremonial context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 60/30)

data.turoyo: Šqəlole. Qrele lu ḥmoro, omər: "Tox mhara." Mhərole lu ḥmoro.
data.translation: antwortete er und erklärte sich bereit, sie zu heiraten. Er rief dem Esel: "Komm, traue sie mir an", und der Esel traute sie.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: officiant with omitted spouse; complete simple narrative.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 85/71)

data.turoyo: Əmmi: "Tox aʕmayna." Omər: "L mune?" Əmmi: "Mḥawele lu malkayḏan kalo lu abro, tox mhara." Omər: "Kaṯino."
data.translation: "Komm mit uns!" baten sie. "Wesshalb?" "Unser König hat seinem Sohne eine Braut heimgeführt, komm und traue sie."

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: king’s son and requested officiant.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (107/56)

data.turoyo: mawbəl lu zʕurano w izolux, mhar i nxirayto aʕle
data.translation: nimm diesen Jüngling mit, geh und verheirate die Verlobte mit ihm

rationale: Fifth Imperativ example: explicit fiancée and ʕal-spouse.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
before: antrauen, verheiraten mit (ʕal) (Mädchen) (only in islamic marriage - Shabo; naqdo - for the christians);
after: antrauen, verheiraten mit (ʕal); heiraten (auch reziprok und mit männlichem Partner als Objekt);
rationale: The reciprocal couple at PrS 4/17, male object at 95/57 and explicit Christian priest/baptism at PrS 34/111–113 broaden the participant and ceremony restrictions. Preserve Shabo’s narrower speaker report in a research note rather than as an exceptionless lexical restriction.

summary: The inherited speaker report is: only in islamic marriage - Shabo; naqdo - for the christians. PrS 34/111–113 explicitly has a qašo who baptises a woman and then marries three women to a man. The lexical restriction is therefore qualified, while Shabo’s narrower usage report is preserved here.

mhəlle/mhəḷḷe and mhir- coexist; Infectum mohaṇṇa, gmohaṇṇax, kmuhanno, məhannola and gməhrallux show substantial suffix-related variation. Do not infer another root from the surface loss of r or collapse the marriage root with mhr 2 seal/elect.
The nominal mhoro after dlo is attested three times. It supports Infinitiv, not a secure new Detransitive Preterit. The existing məmhoro Infectum at 95/21 is already cited and is not duplicated.
A plural reciprocal subject is plausible at LuF 1/36 / PrS 4/17; these look like parallel versions of one narrative, so they are not counted as two independent demonstrations of a new sense.

99/120 is not a replacement citation for the inherited two-women example at 99/114: it is a different marriage scene. The reader’s report that 99/114 lacks the verb warrants verification, not an invented fix-citation.
Confirm whether mhərre ḥḏoḏe has the couple as mutual agents or permits an indefinite officiating group. The proposal merges the construction into sense 1 either way.
Confirm active mhirole/mhiroli versus a Detransitive interpretation, particularly with l-spouses in 112/261. No new Detransitive box is asserted from these ambiguous forms.
Are spouse complements ʕam- and l- freely interchangeable with ʕal- in these varieties?
Does the Christian ceremony in PrS 34 reflect narrator-wide use, contact or story-specific wording? How does this compare with Shabo’s narrower report and the Samson retelling?
Verify 99/114 against the source edition and the relationship of prs 163/22, PrS 59/87 and the other parallel two-women episodes before changing any inherited citation.
Confirm the nominal status of mhoro after dlo and the narrative discrepancy at PrS 36/59; neither an unconsummated-marriage meaning nor a finite Detransitive form is securely established.

The acting party may be an officiant, an arranger or a spouse. Direct objects include a bride, a male partner or both partners; ḥḏoḏe expresses mutual marriage. This participant variation does not split the marriage meaning.
Spouse complements are normally ʕal-, but ʕam- at PrS 39/100 and l- at 112/261 are also attested; retain these surface contrasts pending confirmation.
